title: Lesson 21 - FlexCard Best Practices: Design, Data, and Performance

questions.question: A FlexCard displays three fields, but its data source returns a wide record with dozens of fields. What best practice is violated?
options: The data source is not lean, adding payload and render cost
The card has too few elements
The output variables are not mapped
questions.explanation: A best practice is to return only the fields the card uses, because extra fields add payload and render cost. The theme, element count, and output variables are not the issue; the data source is over-fetching.

questions.question: An architect nests many child cards when a single flat card would display the same data. What is the primary concern?
options: Each child adds render and data-fetch cost, slowing the card
The data source is too lean
questions.explanation: Each child FlexCard is a separate instance with its own render and data-fetch cost, so over-nesting slows the card. Render speed, theme, and a lean data source are not the concern; the nesting itself is.

questions.question: A FlexCard works in the editor but fails in production with empty data. What best practice was most likely skipped?
options: Testing the card in its real placement with real data
questions.explanation: A card can fail in production because of input mapping, missing fields, or placement context, so testing in the target environment with real data is a best practice. Theme, element count, and charts do not address production failures.
